chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Yunus, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no area more beloved to Allah than the Sa'ee, because therein every tyrant is humbled.' And it is reported that he was asked, 'Why was the Sa'ee made?' So he said: 'To humble the tyrants.'

key_terms.السَّعْيُ: The Sa'ee, the act of hurrying/walking in the ritual
key_terms.الْمَسْعَى: The Sa'ee, the ritual walking between Safa and Marwa
key_terms.جَبَّارٍ: Tyrant, one who is arrogant and domineering

ai.seo_question: Why is the Sa'ee ritual considered the most beloved area to Allah?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the spiritual significance of Sa'ee as a ritual of humility that specifically subdues the arrogance of the 'tyrants' (al-jabbarin), a term often associated with divine attributes or human oppressors in Shia exegesis. This act is not merely physical movement but a profound demonstration of submission, reinforcing the concept that true nobility lies in lowering oneself before Allah, thereby nullifying the pride of those who consider themselves superior.
